scope: isolated lock-contention probes; not demonstrated signed-customer failures

matview_refresh.old_behavior: SKIPPED_LOCK_HELD retried at 1s with max_retries=10; a lock held longer than the 10-attempt budget left the last refresh stale until another event arrived.
matview_refresh.new_behavior: Both matview tasks have max_retries=None; lock-held retries use capped exponential countdown 1,2,4,8,16,30s and never exhaust. The task itself remains the durable retry chain; no external event is required.
tests: attempt=12 still requests retry with countdown=30 and max_retries=None
matview_refresh.deployment_consequence: Longer legitimate lock contention delays the refresh by at most the capped interval; it no longer strands the last update permanently.

jwt_verification.old_behavior: When another process held the PostgreSQL refresh lease past the bounded unknown-kid poll, the verifier returned the cached ring and a token carrying the rotated kid was rejected until a later request happened to retry.
jwt_verification.new_behavior: If the refreshed ring still lacks the requested kid, the verifier reads the sanctioned source-of-truth ring directly for this request and updates its local cache. It does not write the shared cache while another process owns the lease.
tests: stale shared ring returned; source read once; rotated token accepted
jwt_verification.deployment_consequence: Unknown-kid verification is no longer left stale by a long-held refresh lease; the source ring remains the authority.

limits: The lock-contention probes are isolated unit/contract probes, not signed-customer failures.

The production-lane advisory-lock proof covers a 5-second real PostgreSQL lock; the 12-attempt retry behavior is proven at the task-policy boundary, not by holding a lock for 12 seconds in a live container.
No threshold was lowered; the retry budget was made durable rather than bounded.
